clue.text: Semitic idiom initially included in Chambers, revised version?

definitions.text: Semitic idiom initially included in Chambers, revised version?

indicators.note: a revised version of a text is a reworked one, so the pooled letters are rearranged
initially asks for the opening letter of each of the two words idiom and included

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a new edition of Chambers dictionary has slipped in a Hebrew turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'idiom' and 'included' (I, I); 'revised version' rearranges those with CHAMBERS. The whole clue is also the definition: such an idiom could indeed be listed in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebraicism is a phrase or construction borrowed from Hebrew, a Semitic tongue.

clue.text: Erstwhile Archbishop to sing somehow at start of evensong

parts.note: to hum is to sing after a fashion, with closed lips

indicators.note: at the start of a word means its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A former archbishop hums his way into the beginning of evening prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal Basil Hume was Archbishop of Westminster until 1999.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil Hume led the Catholic archdiocese of Westminster, hence a former archbishop.

clue.text: When to start one, principally being on November fifth? That's about right

definitions.text: When to start one, principally being on November fifth? That's about right

indicators.note: principally points to the leading letter of each of the four words that follow

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
re is a Latin-derived word for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the fifth of November is the time to light one, and is told that's about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principally' takes B, O, N, F from 'being on November fifth'; add I and RE. Guy Fawkes Night, 5 November, is when Britons light these outdoor fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor fires are lit across Britain on Guy Fawkes Night, 5 November.

clue.text: Washed out yes, and perhaps by the start of Lent

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something has been washed out, yes, perhaps as Lent begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent begins on the Wednesday when penitents are marked with ashes.

clue.text: In a difficult position, like Jenny Colgan's bookshop?

definitions.meaning: trapped with no way out, like an animal at bay
Jenny Colgan wrote the novel The Bookshop on the Corner, so her shop is, whimsically, at a street angle

explanation.definitionFit: Trapped means hemmed in; and a shop set at a street angle is jokingly described the same way.

clue.text: Attempt to include a bass at the start of Barbiere? That's contemptible

indicators.note: to include means the attempt holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a shy is a try or throw, as in a coconut shy
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

indicators.note: at the start of picks the first letter of the word Barbiere

explanation.surface: A singer tries to get a bass into the opening of Rossini's Barber of Seville, and is scorned.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby conduct is mean and dishonourable, deserving scorn.

clue.text: Work of Andrei Rublev, I learn

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Someone studies the work of the great Russian painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrei Rublev was a medieval Russian painter of sacred images such as the Trinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Rublev painted religious panel images for Orthodox churches.

clue.text: Mythical creature dispatched, we hear, to a Chaldean town

indicators.note: we hear says the preceding word is to be taken as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: dispatched means sent off
Ur of the Chaldees is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A mythical beast is packed off to ancient Mesopotamia.
explanation.definitionFit: The half-man, half-horse of Greek myth is a fabulous creature.

clue.text: Complete set of directions to street and singular places to buy the TLS

parts.note: the four compass points north, east, west, south
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Directions to a street with places selling the literary paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiosks selling newspapers and periodicals stock the TLS.

clue.text: Here you'll find Narnia, much translated into an Asian language

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: C S Lewis's Narnia, rendered into an East Asian tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tungusic language of the Manchu people of north-east China.

clue.text: So new men finally formed a topic for him

definitions.text: So new men finally formed a topic for him

indicators.note: formed means shaped anew, so the letters are rearranged
finally takes the last letter of each of the words new and men

explanation.surface: A novelist found his subject in the rise of a new class of men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives W and N; 'formed' rearranges them with SO. C P Snow wrote the novel The New Men, so they were indeed his topic.
explanation.definitionFit: C P Snow's novel The New Men took up that very subject.

clue.text: French lovers or those who preferred a Spanish dictator?

definitions.meaning: people who love France and its culture

definitions.text: those who preferred a Spanish dictator?
definitions.meaning: read as admirers of General Franco, the Spanish dictator

explanation.definitionFit: Admirers of France; and, split as Franco plus philes, admirers of Franco.

clue.text: Pretend to sing two notes written for a Wagnerian tenor

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
me is an alternative spelling of mi in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: Two notes are written for a tenor in a Wagner opera, who only pretends to sing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written for a Wagnerian tenor' adds a second definition: Mime is the tenor dwarf in Wagner's Ring cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To mouth words without voicing them, as performers do to a recording.

clue.text: May breed perhaps at start of summer and times of prayer

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters may be arranged otherwise
at the start of a word means its first letter

explanation.surface: Animals may breed at the beginning of summer, and the devout pray.
explanation.definitionFit: Ember days are set days of fasting and prayer in the Western church calendar.

clue.text: Poem to perform, everyone individually including part of speech

parts.note: to do something is to perform it
a verb is a part of speech
each means every one taken separately

explanation.surface: Instructions for reciting a poem with everyone taking a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover Beach is Matthew Arnold's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold's famous lyric of 1867 on faith's retreating tide.

clue.text: Source of flowers her lover's given to Hero at last

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word Hero

parts.note: in Greek legend Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his love Hero

explanation.surface: Hero's lover brings her flowers at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean evergreen shrub bearing showy pink or white blooms.

clue.text: Giordano's man depicted in grand realism

indicators.note: depicted in says the name is shown inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Giordano's hero portrayed with sweeping realism.
explanation.walkthrough: Umberto Giordano wrote the opera Andrea Chénier, about the French poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Giordano's opera about the poet Chénier.

clue.text: McDermid's prayer for Br nnhilde?

parts.note: Val McDermid is the Scottish crime novelist
the Kyrie is the Lord, have mercy prayer of the Mass

explanation.surface: The crime writer offers a prayer for Wagner's warrior maiden.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Brünnhilde, whose u-umlaut is missing as held.
explanation.definitionFit: Brünnhilde is chief of the warrior maidens of Norse myth in Wagner's Ring.

clue.text: Meredith's antihero, for example, is absorbed by a set of books

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: absorbed by means the word is is taken inside the following letters

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: George Meredith's antihero is lost in a set of books.
explanation.walkthrough: George Meredith's novel The Egoist has the self-centred Sir Willoughby Patterne at its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Meredith's novel The Egoist names its vain central figure by that type.

clue.text: Religious books were sufficient for Manfred's castle

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament
ran to means stretched to or were enough for

explanation.surface: Religious volumes sufficed for a Gothic lord's castle.
explanation.walkthrough: In Horace Walpole's Gothic novel The Castle of Otranto, the castle belongs to Manfred.
explanation.definitionFit: Walpole's Gothic novel sets its villain Manfred in that Italian stronghold.

clue.text: One who hates operetta or diva say perhaps? Not I!

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of or diva say, with one I set aside as Not I says, are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asked whether he'd say opera or diva, an operetta-hater cries 'Not I!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not I!' sets one letter aside from the pooled words before 'perhaps' shuffles them. A Savoyard is in fact a Gilbert and Sullivan devotee, so 'hates' reads as irony.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoyards are devotees of the Gilbert and Sullivan comic operas staged at the Savoy Theatre.

clue.text: Stoppard play in which a scoundrel bursts into song

indicators.note: bursts into means one word forces its way inside the other

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: In a Tom Stoppard play, a rogue suddenly breaks into song.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Stoppard's 1993 play set in a country house across two centuries.

clue.text: Experience yen about Rex, but get Laurence instead..

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first letters surround the second

parts.note: to have is to experience something
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king
Y is the abbreviation for the yen currency

explanation.surface: Wanting Rex Harrison for a role but having to settle for another actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Harvey was the actor of Room at the Top; Rex Harrison is the misleading neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the actor Laurence Harvey.

clue.text: A dance in a form of drama by an Austrian composer

parts.note: Alban Berg was the Austrian composer of Wozzeck
a mask, or masque, is a courtly entertainment of verse, music and dance

explanation.surface: A dance worked into a masque by Alban Berg.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic dance, as performed by the mechanicals in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Abandon topless Finn

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to chuck something is to give it up

explanation.surface: A Finn is told to drop the bare-chested look.
explanation.definitionFit: Huck Finn is Mark Twain's boy hero, Huckleberry.

clue.text: … because he was an expert in Arthurian legend

parts.note: as can mean because

explanation.surface: Someone is introduced as an authority on King Arthur.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Ashe wrote widely on the historical Arthur; the leading dots tie the clue to the one before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey Ashe was a British historian of the King Arthur tales.

clue.text: Overture to Rosamond included by an English composer

indicators.note: included by means the letter goes inside the word an
the overture to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Opening music for Rosamond, written by an English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne wrote the opera Rosamond (1733).
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne, eighteenth-century writer of Rule, Britannia!

clue.text: Always happy to be given directions to Hiaasen country

parts.note: ever means always
glad means happy
E and S are the compass points east and south

explanation.surface: Glad to be pointed the way to the setting of Carl Hiaasen's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Hiaasen sets his comic crime novels in the Florida swamps.

clue.text: Author of gung-ho odes

indicators.note: of here means made of, so the name is drawn from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A writer of enthusiastic odes.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hood wrote odes, including his Ode to Melancholy.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hood was a Victorian poet and humorist.

clue.text: "He checked the time. He'd been in for five hours (William Gibson, Neuromancer)

definitions.text: "He checked the time. He'd been in for five hours (William Gibson, Neuromancer)

parts.words: "He checked the time. He'd been in for five hours (William Gibson, Neuromancer)
parts.note: a quotation with a word missing after in: the virtual realm the novel's hacker jacks into

explanation.surface: A quotation from Gibson's novel with a gap to fill.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibson coined the term for the computer-network realm his hacker enters.
